knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Non-finite gradient inputs can trigger backend assertions during backward
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Backward implementations for differentiable operators may assume finite floating-point values, and non-finite inputs combined with requires_grad=True can violate device-side assertions or invariant checks, causing crashes.

risk_dimensions.shape: No fixed shape boundary; non-finite values in any tensor shape may trigger the issue.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Floating-point dtypes capable of representing NaN or Inf, such as float16, bfloat16, float32, and float64.
risk_dimensions.device: CUDA and potentially other accelerator backends where assertions are device-side.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: requires_grad=True and backward invocation; repeated backward calls may further exercise cached gradient state.

failure_mechanism.description: Backward or gradient kernels may contain assertions or assume finite inputs; non-finite values can cause device-side assertion failures and process termination.

input_exploration: Introduce NaN or Inf into floating-point tensors that require gradients.
Vary the count and position of non-finite values.
Test different floating-point dtypes capable of representing non-finite values.
Run on CUDA and invoke one or more backward passes.
constraint_awareness: Execution should be on a device backend that can assert, such as CUDA.
Non-finite values must be present before the differentiable operation.
oracle_strategy: Detect CUDA assert failures or process termination during backward.
Monitor for device-side assertion signals after backward is invoked.

transferability.reason: The principle applies broadly to differentiable operators whose backward kernels may assume finite floating-point inputs, but the manifestation and severity depend on backend implementations and specific gradient kernels.

important_considerations: Focus on gradient-state and numerical edge interactions rather than a single API.
Explore operators that compute gradients on CUDA with non-finite floating-point inputs.
Consider repeated backward calls and gradient accumulation behavior.
Use non-finite values placed in varied tensor positions and shapes.
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that mutate floating-point tensor values to include NaN or Inf, set requires_grad=True, run differentiable operations on CUDA, invoke backward, and detect device assertion or crash signals. Avoid hard-coding one specific API or exact reproduction values.
